chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever starts his morning with twenty-one red raisins will not fall ill except with the sickness of death, if Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of eating red raisins in the morning according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic tradition of *al-tasbah* (morning consumption), specifically linking the number twenty-one to the completion of a lunar cycle, a numerological significance often explored in Shia hadith sciences. It underscores the holistic view of health in Shia tradition, where dietary habits are seen as a means of preserving bodily vitality until the appointed time of death (*al-maut al-mu'ajjal*). The specificity of 'red raisins' (*zabibah hamra'*) reflects the emphasis on selecting high-quality, natural foods for their therapeutic properties.
